Subject: MSA & Order Form – starting paperwork

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — Morph o's exec team liked the throughput numbers. Procurement asked me to get the MSA and order form ball rolling so legal can review before our pilot start. Can you send over your standard MSA and an editable order form? Two immediate asks from our side:

- We need to confirm data residency (US-only) and whether you accept a customer-managed KMS.
- Our legal lead will want to see any high-level redlines you typically accept (IP, indemnity, liability cap).

Attaching a one-pager of expected volumes and a tentative contract start date (not a PO). Happy to set a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Brian

Morpho Health

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form – starting paperwork

Hi Brian — great to hear. Looping in Marissa (contracts lead) and Rishi (commercial) to help.

I've attached Redwood's standard MSA and a blank order form template to speed things up. To keep the review efficient, please confirm the following items and we can prioritize redlines accordingly:

1) Billing & PO: billing contact name + email, whether you'll route via centralized PO (and PO number format).
2) Data residency & KMS: confirm US-only requirement and whether you need customer-managed KMS. We support external KMS via our Private offering — may need SOW/Private deployment conversation.
3) SLA expectation: target p99 latency / uptime goals you need for pilot and production.
4) Insurance & indemnity: let us know your target liability cap; we usually see requests to move from our standard $5M cap.
5) Security evidence: will you run an intake questionnaire (we can provide SOC2 report and penetration test summary)? Please share your vendor security form if you have one.

Next steps I propose:
- You return answers to the 5 items above and your procurement contact.
- We accept a short redline window: Marissa will flag high-priority commercial items; Rishi will own order form economics.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Template_v1.docx (docx), Redwood_OrderForm_Template.xlsx (xlsx)

Laura Bennett

Laura / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers below inline: 

1) Billing & PO: billing@morophhealth.com is the billing contact (POs come through later, format will be PO-#####).
2) Data residency & KMS: we require US-only. KMS — we prefer customer-managed; can you confirm whether Redwood's private package is required or if hosted can accommodate YubiKey-managed keys during pilot?
3) SLA expectation: pilot needs 99.5% uptime and p95 latency < 400ms for typical gen-2 workloads.
4) Insurance & indemnity: our legal prefers a $10M cap; they are open to negotiation on specific carve-outs.
5) Security evidence: attaching Morpho vendor security form.

Attaching: Morpho_Security_Questionnaire.pdf and draft order form (Morpho_OrderForm_Draft.pdf). Also happy to schedule a 30-min sync if you want to walk Rishi through expected consumption patterns.

Brian — thanks for the prompt responses and the questionnaire. We've started an internal thread to triage the asks. Quick update and next steps: 

- KMS/Data residency: Rishi: can you confirm whether pilot can be supported on hosted infra with customer-managed KMS (we may need to provision a Private trial if not).
- Liability cap: Marissa will propose a counter to the $10M ask. Typically we keep the cap at $5M but provide limited carve-outs; we'll include rationale.
- SLA: we'll confirm which guarantees we can reasonably commit for pilot vs. production.

I've uploaded an annotated MSA with Marissa's first-pass comments to the shared drive (link below) and attached for your convenience. The annotated MSA highlights the three areas where we typically push back: liability cap, indemnity reciprocity, and data handling. If you can review and indicate priority order (which clauses matter most to Morph o), we'll fast-track negotiations.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed (tomorrow): Marissa to send annotated MSA (first pass) — done (attached).
- Thu: commercial alignment on order form economics (Rishi will share a short spreadsheet).
- Fri: 30-min sync if needed to iron out any term-level blockers.
